clue.text: Traffic force cut by a couple of thousand

indicators.note: a word cut by something has that thing driven into its middle

parts.note: to coerce is to force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: Some traffic police unit has had its numbers cut by two thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' reads like road vehicles, but here it means trade. 'cut by' signals one word driven into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in the sense of trading goods is a synonym for commerce.

clue.text: He was but as the is in June, heard, not regarded. Shakespeare (King Henry IV)

definitions.text: He was but as the is in June, heard, not regarded. Shakespeare (King Henry IV)

parts.words: He was but as the is in June, heard, not regarded
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing after 'the': a bird often heard in June but rarely seen

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's history play about a king, with a word to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue leaves a gap after 'the' for the missing word of the quotation from Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird named in the speech is one whose call is famous in early summer.

clue.text: One may follow the guys, being a pest

indicators.note: one piece follows, or comes after, the other

parts.note: guys are men
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone who trails after the men can be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' sits at the start of the surface but comes last; 'may follow' says where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace, informally, is an annoying person, a nuisance.

clue.text: Able to bring parking into use

indicators.note: into signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: to exert strength is to use it
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Being able to make a car park usable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts P inside EXERT, giving EX-P-ERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert is an adjective meaning skilled or capable.

clue.text: Agree to write some letters

definitions.meaning: to agree is to match or tally with something
to write letters is to exchange them by post with someone

explanation.surface: Agreeing to write a few letters to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to match or tally and to exchange letters by post.

clue.text: Like a knife for a youngster confined to bed

indicators.note: someone confined to a place is kept inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A description of something knife-like suitable for a child who is laid up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined to' signals a container: the youngster is kept inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife has a blade, so anything with a blade is like one.

clue.text: The doctor and model in general drink

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the word for general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A doctor and a fashion model, both in general, having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun beside 'doctor' but is a verb, rearranging 'and'; 'in' then places both pieces within the general's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink made with lemons.

clue.text: The underworld have the answer-vanish!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
to solve a problem is to find the answer to it

explanation.surface: A melodramatic cry that hell has the solution and should disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to melt away or disappear.

clue.text: Feels hopelessness is spread by agitation

indicators.note: agitation stirs things up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Despair spreading through a crowd that is agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by agitation' rearranges IS SPREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel hopeless is to lose all hope, the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Scheme to study an outstanding feature of the church

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a spire stands out above a church building

explanation.surface: A plan to examine a church's most striking architectural feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme is to plot secretly together, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Assume breakdown causes diversion

indicators.note: a breakdown takes a word apart so its letters can be reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Presuming that a mechanical breakdown will lead to a traffic detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' rearranges ASSUME.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to provide entertainment, or diversion, for them.

clue.text: Showed up a top man — successfully treated outside right

parts.note: OC, Officer Commanding, is the top man of a military unit

indicators.note: one word sitting outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a patient successfully treated is cured

explanation.surface: A senior figure turned up after being cured of whatever ailed him on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a top man' suggests a boss; in crosswords the commanding officer is a standard source of these two letters. 'outside' wraps only the treated piece round 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurred happened or appeared, much as something that showed up did.

clue.text: Article given a record backing in Africa

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for record is read in reverse

parts.note: a log is a record, such as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A newspaper article accompanies a record going into reverse somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns only the record round; the 'a' then follows unchanged. 'in Africa' defines a country there.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies in south-west Africa, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Finding a lever in reverse, turned it on, so causing a leak

indicators.note: in reverse means read backwards
turned suggests the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Discovering that pulling a lever the other way switched something on and caused a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns A LEVER into REVELA; 'turned' rearranges IT ON into TION. 'Finding' and 'so causing' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a disclosure of something secret, as a leak to the press is.

clue.text: Pears cooked with port should be covered

indicators.note: cooked suggests the fruit is prepared and altered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Dover is a ferry port in Kent, England

explanation.surface: A recipe note: pears stewed in port wine ought to be kept under a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges PEARS into SPREA; 'port' looks like the wine but is Dover, the English Channel ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread over a surface has been covered with a layer.

clue.text: Like the finest sailor, can't be fired

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
the best is the finest
OS, ordinary seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An outstanding seaman who cannot lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't be fired' means can't be burnt, not can't be sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fireproof mineral that will not burn.

clue.text: Shooting about fifty for subversive activity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: potting is shooting game, or balls into pockets
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A gun used against about fifty people in some rebellious act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts POTTING around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting means scheming secretly, as conspirators against a government do.

clue.text: The strength of the current

parts.note: reads like a description of a fast-flowing river, but means electrical current measured in amps

explanation.surface: How strongly a river is flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the size of an electric current, measured in amps.

clue.text: The French to some degree into smoother but fiery spirit

indicators.note: into signals pieces going inside another word

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: French words being inserted into some smoothing device, yet producing a fiery being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places both small pieces inside the smoothing tool's name, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the salamander was a creature, or elemental spirit, that lived in fire.

clue.text: Compound a lie is what coordinators do!

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Telling one lie on top of another is how fixers work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' rearranges A LIE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to act as a link between groups, which is a coordinator's job.

clue.text: A way to go on setting the pace

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to go on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A route to follow when someone is leading the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A', 'to' and 'setting the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single long step, a pace.

clue.text: The man who's given a home with royal insignia above it

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed above another comes first

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher on post boxes and the like
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A man given a house marked with the royal crest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'above it' means the royal letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name.

clue.text: Certain evergreen trees can be a source of food

indicators.note: certain here means some of, so only part of the letters of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some kinds of evergreen tree can provide people or animals with something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'evergreen' and 'trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served at a meal, something people eat.

clue.text: The case where care isn't exercised

indicators.note: exercised suggests the letters are worked about and moved around

explanation.surface: A situation in which nobody is being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' rearranges CARE ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, a kind of case for holding things.

clue.text: Hearing about second class of people

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
B is the second grade or class after A

explanation.surface: A court hearing concerning second-class citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TRIAL around B, giving TRI-B-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal means belonging to a tribe, a group of people.

clue.text: Disruptive quartet one's seen in a disreputable place

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
IV is four in Roman numerals
one is I, so one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: A rowdy foursome turns up at a seedy venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' places the Roman four and 'one's' inside the seedy venue, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisive behaviour splits people, disrupting harmony.

clue.text: Autographed fashion design

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A designer garment bearing its creator's signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Autographed means bearing a person's signature.

clue.text: A profitable pastime?

parts.note: the word wanted means both money earned on savings and a hobby, so a hobby that pays fits both senses

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there is a hobby that earns money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hobby that holds attention and the return on money lent.
